source.title: Nonlinear Collaborative Scheme for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Hui-Ling Zhen; Xi Lin; Alan Tang; Zhenhua Li; Qing-Fu Zhang; S. Kwong

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study compares a nonlinear loss scheme with single-loss and linear-loss schemes and reports training and validation accuracy, using a different intervention from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper varies label randomization on CIFAR-10 and reports training and validation accuracy, but does not test full random labeling or report whether held-out accuracy is at chance. It does not test the specific architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, width, sharpness, or example-removal versions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses label randomization inspired by Zhang et al. to evaluate its proposed loss scheme. Its experiments compare training objectives, not any claim version. Partial label corruption with explicit regularization and gradient noise does not establish V1's coexistence of near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting and natural-label generalization. Section VI.A invokes prior sharpness results but supplies no measured sharpness–gap comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical conclusion: the authors report higher training and validation accuracy and smoother curves, including under partial label corruption. It omits their theoretical claims of smaller KL divergence, a connection to optimizing a differentially private PAC-Bayes prior, and a tighter PAC-Bayes bound.
record.recipe_differences: The study changes the training objective by combining losses nonlinearly; it does not reproduce the interventions in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, network family, label-randomization level, loss scheme, and regularization parameter differ across experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report better training and validation accuracy and smoother curves with nonlinear CE–MSE collaboration than with CE alone or linear collaboration, on original CIFAR labels and partially randomized CIFAR-10 labels. Regularization settings differ across several comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nonlinear combinations of classification losses can improve accuracy and training-curve smoothness in the tested ResNet and DenseNet settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The paper argues that optimizing its nonlinear objective corresponds to optimizing a data-dependent PAC-Bayes prior and yields a tighter bound than the local-entropy formulation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the paper's assumptions, nonlinear loss collaboration improves its proposed PAC-Bayes bound.

record.problems: Accuracy curves are presented as figures without numerical values in the text. The paper varies regularization parameters across schemes and states that loss-function choice can change experimental results. Random-label experiments use partial randomization only.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted; 36 rows retained, within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed fully random labels, chance held-out performance with those labels, and coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error; no width sweep.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under specified tuning budgets; mentioning optimizer choices supplies no such comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance; Section VI.A cites earlier findings only.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization regimes.
Measured association between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps, and ranking against alternative measures. Section VI.A supplies a theoretical motivation, not this comparison.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All 36 rows describe the proposed method or its comparators and should be excluded from evidence for V1–V8. Their observed/partial states encode relative method performance, not the named claim effects. Figure 3 also contains validation curves omitted by the record despite its statement that no rows were omitted; these do not warrant a version-specific missing entry. Exact curve values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests 20% and 80% label randomization, not fixed fully random labels; it does not establish near-perfect random-label fit, chance held-out accuracy, or compare the same recipe on natural versus fully random labels.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
